title: TravelAgent: Generative agents in the built environment
audit_note: Full text is now local and confirms a strong 3D/L5 interface, but the paper remains single-agent navigation and wayfinding rather than stable Core multi-agent social behavior.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
audit_note: The small-town sandbox remains the clearest Core anchor for situated social behavior, memory, and emergent coordination.

title: Generative agent-based modeling with actions grounded in physical, social, or digital space using Concordia
audit_note: Core as an environment-architecture anchor. Later coding should split concrete interface variants rather than flattening the whole framework into one representation level.

title: Affordable Generative Agents
audit_note: Keeps both agent-environment and inter-agent interaction explicit, but the paper is more about scalable believable interaction than about a new environment representation.

title: Artificial Leviathan: Exploring Social Evolution of LLM Agents Through the Lens of Hobbesian Social Contract Theory
audit_note: A strong sandbox-society paper with explicit conflict, cooperation, and social-order emergence.

title: Project Sid: Many-agent simulations toward AI civilization
audit_note: Large-scale civilization simulation in a game world. Core is stable, but the exact agent-facing representation and action interface still need careful extraction.

title: OASIS: Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations with One Million Agents
audit_note: Retained in Core as a reusable environment-architecture anchor rather than as a reason to reopen broad digital-platform expansion.

title: Lyfe Agents: Generative agents for low-cost real-time social interactions
audit_note: 3D virtual environment, local interaction, and movement are already confirmed.

title: Spontaneous Emergence of Agent Individuality Through Social Interactions in Large Language Model-Based Communities
audit_note: The 50 by 50 grid world and community-level norm formation make this a strong broadened-core paper.

title: Real world community oriented high-definition social simulation: Combining reinforcement learning and large language models
audit_note: Important for realistic built-environment social simulation, but later coding should capture the exact GIS, BIM, and Unreal observation-action pipeline.

title: SimWorld: An Open-ended Realistic Simulator for Autonomous Agents in Physical and Social Worlds
audit_note: Rich embodied and social environment with multiple interface configurations. Core is stable, but one flat coding row would hide important variation.

title: Large-language-model-driven agents for fire evacuation simulation in a cellular automata environment
audit_note: Local pdf2text extraction and method review confirm 10 agents, a cell-semantic 2D automaton rendered into text prompts, nearby communication, and observed evacuation outcomes.

title: When agents learn to think: Large language model-enhanced agent-based modeling for crowd evacuation in disaster scenarios
audit_note: Local pdf2text extraction and method review confirm a population-scale GIS road-network evacuation system with memory, hazard observations, nearby communication, baseline comparison, and report-level validation.

title: CitySim: Modeling Urban Behaviors and City Dynamics with Large-Scale LLM-Driven Agent Simulation
audit_note: Explicit urban districts, place functions, mobility, and city-level collective dynamics make this a stable Core paper.

title: MineLand: Simulating Large-Scale Multi-Agent Interactions with Limited Multimodal Senses and Physical Needs
audit_note: Full-text sanity review confirms bounded RGB/audio/touch perception, distance-limited communication, physical needs, cooperation, competition, and observed collective behavior in a multi-agent Minecraft world.

title: GATSim: Urban Mobility Simulation with Generative Agents
audit_note: Full-text sanity review confirms a transport-network environment, spatial-temporal memory retrieval, adaptive mobility planning, and observed macroscopic traffic patterns. This row is accepted conservatively as population-level observed-effect Core evidence.

title: An LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Simulation Framework for Coupled Epidemic-Economic Dynamics
audit_note: Markdown full-text review confirms a rectangular 2D city grid, role-specific agents, physical contact-distance transmission, movement/work/consumption actions, and observed epidemic-economic trajectories across policy scenarios.

title: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
audit_note: Core placement is secure, but the exact agent-accessible spatial representation still needs method-level coding rather than title- or abstract-level inference.
